title: Act Bravely
coreMove: Quiet courage means letting the body feel fear, then doing the needed thing with less heat: pause, name the duty, and step without needing drama.

exampleSpecs.stakes: respond to a visible failure without letting speed replace judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A public blame request is slowed by confirmed facts and restraint.

exampleSpecs.audience: volunteers who want courage to feel dramatic
exampleSpecs.stakes: see repeated service as courage instead of mere helpfulness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one closely observed kitchen moment teaches repeated bodily duty

exampleSpecs.stakes: locate the one moment when dramatic action replaced judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A school security lesson rebuilds a response around evidence instead of accusation.

exampleSpecs.stakes: correct a performative speech before it harms the cause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A council speaker keeps dissent firm by changing the next sentence.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders choosing a measured emergency response
exampleSpecs.stakes: make the written recommendation brave without making it flashy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A hospital operations lead chooses a narrow pause with named duties.

exampleSpecs.audience: staff deciding how to carry public commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: see how waiting for fear to vanish differs from acting with steadiness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A public statement is signed while discomfort remains present.
